name: War Inc: Rising Roulette vs Fusion — Which Is Better for Your Gems?
title: War Inc: Rising Roulette vs Fusion — Cost Breakdown at Every Breakpoint | War Inc: Rising Wiki
meta_description: Detailed cost comparison of the Roulette and Fusion systems in War Inc: Rising. See exactly how many mystics you get at every breakpoint — 10, 25, 50, 100, 200 spins — and why Fusion gives you 22 mystics per 10,000 gems.
author: War Inc Wiki Team
excerpt: The Roulette and Fusion are the two main ways to spend gems on mystic heroes in War Inc: Rising. This guide breaks down the exact cost per mystic at every roulette breakpoint and compares it to fusion, so you can decide which method fits your stage of the game.

sections.heading: How the Roulette Works
sections.content:
The Roulette (also called the Wheel) costs 100 gems per spin. It has guaranteed milestone rewards at fixed intervals, plus random mystic drops from the spin outcomes.

Fixed milestone rewards:
- 10 spins: 1 guaranteed mystic hero
- 25 spins: 500 gems refund
- 50 spins: 1 guaranteed mystic hero
- 100 spins: 2 guaranteed mystic heroes
- 200 spins: 500 forge stones

The displayed mystic probability is 4%, but this is misleading. The true breakdown is 0.5% chance of 2 mystic cards and 3.5% chance of 1 mystic card. The effective rate is 3.5% per spin for a single mystic card.

The Roulette is designed to feel rewarding because of the milestone chests, but the cost per mystic increases at every breakpoint due to diminishing returns.

sections.heading: Cost Per Mystic at Every Breakpoint
sections.content:
Here is the exact cost analysis for each roulette milestone. All calculations use the true 3.5% probability per spin.

10 spins (1,000 gems, 1 guaranteed mystic): You get exactly 1 mystic from the milestone chest. With 3.5% probability, you have roughly a 30% chance of getting 1 additional mystic from the spins themselves. Expected total: 1.35 mystics. Effective cost per mystic: 1,000 / 1.35 = roughly 740 gems. This is the cheapest cost per mystic on the Roulette.

25 spins (2,500 gems, 500 refund = 2,000 net, still 1 guaranteed): The 25-spin milestone does not give a mystic, just 500 gems back. Expected mystics from random drops: roughly 0.875 (25 × 3.5%). Total expected: 1.875 mystics. Net cost: 2,000 gems. Effective cost per mystic: 2,000 / 1.875 = roughly 1,067 gems. The cost per mystic jumps significantly because you paid 1,000 more gems for no guaranteed mystic.

50 spins (5,000 gems, 1,500 net with refund, 2 guaranteed): Expected random mystics: roughly 1.75 (50 × 3.5%). Total expected: 3.75 mystics. Net cost: roughly 4,500 gems (accounting for the 500 gem refund at 25). Effective cost per mystic: 4,500 / 3.75 = roughly 1,200 gems. 

100 spins (10,000 gems, 9,500 net with refund, 4 guaranteed): Expected random mystics: roughly 3.5 (100 × 3.5%). Total expected: 7.5 mystics. Net cost: roughly 9,500 gems. Effective cost per mystic: 9,500 / 7.5 = roughly 1,267 gems.

200 spins (20,000 gems, 19,500 net, 4 guaranteed + forge stones): Expected random mystics: roughly 7.0 (200 × 3.5%). Total expected: 11 mystics. Net cost: roughly 19,500 gems. Effective cost per mystic: 19,500 / 11 = roughly 1,773 gems. This is the worst cost per mystic on the Roulette.

Key insight: the 10-spin breakpoint has the best cost per mystic at roughly 740 gems. Every breakpoint after 10 gets progressively more expensive. The 200-spin breakpoint costs more than double per mystic compared to 10 spins.

sections.heading: How Fusion Compares at Every Spending Level
sections.content:
Fusion has no randomness — every mystic costs exactly 450 gems. The more you spend, the more you get. There are no diminishing returns.

At 1,000 gems (same as 10 spins): Fusion gives you 2.22 mystic cards (1,000 / 450). The Roulette gives you roughly 1.35. Fusion wins by 64%.

At 2,000 gems (same as 25 spins net): Fusion gives you 4.44 mystic cards. The Roulette gives you roughly 1.875. Fusion wins by 137%.

At 4,500 gems (same as 50 spins net): Fusion gives you 10 mystic cards. The Roulette gives you roughly 3.75. Fusion wins by 167%.

At 9,500 gems (same as 100 spins net): Fusion gives you 21.1 mystic cards. The Roulette gives you roughly 7.5. Fusion wins by 181%.

At 19,500 gems (same as 200 spins net): Fusion gives you 43.3 mystic cards. The Roulette gives you roughly 11. Fusion wins by 294%.

The gap widens with every breakpoint because fusion has linear cost scaling while the Roulette has diminishing returns. At every spending level, fusion gives you roughly 2x to 4x more mystic cards than the Roulette.

sections.heading: The Quality Difference — Why Roulette Mystics Are Better
sections.content:
There is one important caveat: the mystics available through fusion are not the same as the mystics available through the Roulette.

Fusion mystics come from a fixed pool of 7 heroes. They are good but not top-tier. They are designed to be solid, reliable options that work in any team composition. They do not include the game's strongest mystics.

Roulette mystics include the game's top-tier heroes — Radiant Warrior, Bone Marksman, Necromancer, Frost Queen, and others that are simply stronger than the fusion pool. A level 4 Roulette mystic like Radiant Warrior can outperform a level 6 fusion mystic in many situations.

This is the trade-off: fusion gives you quantity and reliability. The Roulette gives you quality and potential. If you are building your initial roster, fusion is better because having 7 level 6 mystics is better than having 2 level 4 Roulette mystics. But if you already have a full fusion team, the Roulette is the only path to the top-tier heroes that define the endgame meta.

sections.heading: Roulette Breakpoint Recommendations
sections.content:
Based on the cost-per-mystic analysis and your progression stage, here is when to stop at each breakpoint.

10 spins: Recommended for everyone. This is the single best value on the Roulette. At roughly 740 gems per mystic, it is competitive with fusion. Every player should do 10 spins on every wheel that features a mystic they might want. The cost is only 1,000 gems.

25 spins: Do not stop here. This is the worst value breakpoint on the Roulette. You pay roughly 1,067 gems per mystic — almost 50% more than the 10-spin breakpoint. The 500 gem refund is a trap that encourages you to keep spinning. Only go past 10 if you are committed to reaching 50.

50 spins: Minimum recommended breakpoint for dedicated Roulette pushing. You get 2 guaranteed mystics plus roughly 1.75 from random drops. The cost per mystic is roughly 1,200 gems. Only go to 50 if you have a solid fusion roster already and are chasing specific top-tier heroes.

100 spins: Recommended for mid-game and late-game players with a strong fusion base. You get 4 guaranteed mystics plus roughly 3.5 from random drops. The cost per mystic of roughly 1,267 gems is still reasonable for the quality of heroes available. Budget roughly 10,000 gems.

200 spins: Not recommended for any player. The cost per mystic jumps to roughly 1,773 gems — the worst value on the board. The 500 forge stones are not worth the additional cost. Only consider this if you are a heavy spender who has maxed everything else and specifically needs forge stones.

sections.heading: The Verdict — Use Both at the Right Time
sections.content:
The optimal gem spending strategy uses both systems at different stages of the game, not one or the other.

Stage 1 — Early game (first 1-3 months): Fusion only. Spend every gem on fusion until you have a full team of fusion mystics at level 6. Do not touch the Roulette beyond the occasional 10-spin. Your goal is roster depth.

Stage 2 — Mid game (3-6 months): Fusion primary, Roulette secondary. Keep building fusion mystics but start doing Roulette 10-spins and occasional 50-spins on good wheels. You now have enough depth to survive the randomness.

Stage 3 — Late game (6+ months): Roulette primary, fusion maintenance. Your fusion roster is complete. Roulette becomes your main gem sink for top-tier heroes. Continue fusion only for specific role fillers or when you have extra legendary cards.

Following this progression path maximizes your gem efficiency at every stage. Players who rush the Roulette in the early game waste thousands of gems on overpriced mystics. Players who never transition to the Roulette in the late game plateau with a roster that cannot compete at the highest levels.

mainEntity.name: How does the Roulette work in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Roulette costs 100 gems per spin with milestone rewards at 10 (1 mystic), 25 (500 gem refund), 50 (1 mystic), 100 (2 mystics), and 200 (forge stones). True mystic drop rate is 3.5% per spin, not the displayed 4%.

mainEntity.name: Which is better — the Roulette or Fusion in War Inc: Rising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fusion is better for building your initial roster at 450 gems per mystic. The Roulette is better for chasing top-tier heroes once you have a solid fusion base. Fusion gives 22 mystics per 10,000 gems; the Roulette gives roughly 8.

mainEntity.name: What is the best breakpoint to stop at on the Roulette?

acceptedAnswer.text: 10 spins is the best value at roughly 740 gems per mystic. 25 spins is the worst value — never stop there. 50 spins is the minimum for dedicated pushes. 100 spins is good for mid-game players. 200 spins is never worth it.

mainEntity.name: How many mystics do you get in 100 Roulette spins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Roughly 7.5 mystics on average. 4 are guaranteed from milestone chests. The remaining 3.5 come from the 3.5% random drop rate across 100 spins. You could get as few as 4 or as many as 12 with extreme luck.

mainEntity.name: Are fusion mystics weaker than Roulette mystics?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, on average. The 7 fusion mystics are solid but not top-tier. Roulette mystics include the game's strongest heroes. A level 4 Roulette mystic can outperform a level 6 fusion mystic. Fusion gives quantity; the Roulette gives quality.
